description: Moved to Brussels to work as an adviser in the European Parliament for the Spanish Socialist MEP Bárbara Dührkop. He had joined the PSOE in 1993.

role: Member of the cabinet of the UN High Representative for Bosnia and Herzegovina
organization: Office of the High Representative (OHR), Bosnia and Herzegovina (High Representative Carlos Westendorp)
description: Worked in the cabinet of the Spanish diplomat Carlos Westendorp, international High Representative in Bosnia and Herzegovina, at the time of the Kosovo war.

organization: Ayuntamiento de Madrid (Madrid City Council), PSOE group
description: Entered the council in May 2004 to fill a PSOE vacancy (he had been 23rd on the 2003 list), as part of opposition leader Trinidad Jiménez's team; re-elected in 2007 and handled opposition work on economy, urban planning and housing. Left the council on becoming a member of Congress.
Taught economic structure and history of economic thought at the private university where he later obtained his doctorate (2012).

role: Member of the Congress of Deputies (diputado) for Madrid
organization: Congreso de los Diputados (IX Legislature), PSOE group
description: Entered Congress to fill the seat left by former economy minister Pedro Solbes; was not re-elected at the November 2011 general election.

role: Member of the Congress of Deputies (diputado) for Madrid
organization: Congreso de los Diputados (X, XI and XII Legislatures), PSOE group
description: Returned to Congress in January 2013 to fill the seat of Cristina Narbona; re-elected heading the PSOE list in Madrid in December 2015 and June 2016. Resigned his seat on 29 October 2016, hours before the vote in which the PSOE group abstained to allow Mariano Rajoy's investiture, which he opposed.

role: Secretary-General of the PSOE and Leader of the Opposition
description: Elected party leader in the first PSOE primary open to all members (July 2014). Led the party in the December 2015 and June 2016 general elections and failed to win investiture in March 2016. Resigned on 1 October 2016 after losing a vote in the party's Federal Committee.

Returned to the leadership after winning the May 2017 primary against Susana Díaz and Patxi López; confirmed at subsequent federal congresses. As of October 2026 he remains Secretary-General and is the PSOE's candidate for the 29 November 2026 general election.

role: President of the Government of Spain (Presidente del Gobierno)
description: Appointed after the motion of no confidence against Mariano Rajoy succeeded on 1 June 2018 (Real Decreto 353/2018). Continued in office after the April 2019 election (Real Decreto 336/2019), was re-invested on 7 January 2020 heading a PSOE–Unidas Podemos coalition (Real Decreto 1/2020) and again on 16 November 2023 heading a PSOE–Sumar coalition (Real Decreto 828/2023). On 5 October 2026 he dissolved the Cortes Generales (Real Decreto 806/2026, BOE 6 October 2026) and called a general election for 29 November 2026; under the Constitution his government will continue in an acting (en funciones) capacity after that election until a new government takes office.

role: Member of the Congress of Deputies (diputado) for Madrid
organization: Congreso de los Diputados (XIII, XIV and XV Legislatures), Socialist group
description: Elected heading the PSOE list in Madrid in April 2019, November 2019 and July 2023 (registered for the XV Legislature on 9 August 2023). His mandate ended with the dissolution of Congress published on 6 October 2026.

Elected president of the worldwide federation of social-democratic parties at its congress in Madrid, succeeding George Papandreou. Declared in his Congress register of interests as an unpaid position.
